qualitative_or_quantitative_description.value: A high density of dislocations is decorated around the nanotwinned region, contributing to dislocation-nanotwin interaction that reduces the mean free paths of mobile dislocations (twinning-induced plasticity); twin boundaries decorated by multiple stacking faults.
Numerous ~30 nm ZrC particles distributed in FCC grain interior effectively inhibit dislocation movement (precipitation/Orowan strengthening).

slip_behavior.value: At minor plastic deformation planar slip (dislocations) is initially activated in the FCC matrix; after severe deformation a high density of slip bands forms along {111} planes, and nanotwins (~20 nm in size) form during heavy deformation.

phase_evolution.value: Partial recrystallization during 900 °C/5 min annealing; Zr solute drag and Zener pinning of ZrC retard recrystallization, producing the bimodal FCC (CG+FG) heterogeneous grain structure.

interface_notes.value: At 2 % global strain the CG zones and FG/CG hetero-interfaces experience high local strain while FG zones remain nearly undeformed (strain partitioning); at 8 % global strain FG zones also accumulate strain. Hardness difference between soft CG and hard FG zones drives geometrically necessary dislocation (GND) generation and HDI strengthening.

Strengthening budget of the Zr0.50 steel: grain-boundary strengthening + HDI strengthening ~300 MPa and ZrC precipitation (Orowan) strengthening 108 MPa.
Stacking fault energy (SFE) of the FCC matrix in the Zr0.50 steel is estimated to be ~55 mJ/m^2 (Supplementary text S1).
Deformation nanotwins in the Zr0.50 steel are ~20 nm in size, with twin boundaries decorated by multiple stacking faults, indicating formation from multiple Shockley partial dislocations.
ZrC precipitates in the Zr0.50 steel are ~30 nm in size with a fraction of 0.006 (~0.6 %) after 900 °C annealing, consistent with the Thermo-Calc calculation.
The {111} slip bands and nanotwinning in the deformed Zr0.50 steel provide additional strengthening and enable twinning-induced plasticity (TWIP).
